data.title: bn-1r9c: mess-bench live-tail / global-position read workload
data.description:
Adds crates/mess-bench/src/workloads/live_tail.rs, the suite's first workload to touch the global read path at all. bn-3hm4 found zero read_global / read_global_page calls (hence zero ActiveIndex::global_range) across all nine existing workloads, and no multi-stream read_stream paging.

Structure mirrors bn-1dlb reader_contention: solo reference plus loaded pass, same host, same run. Four passes over one corpus: catch-up (1 vs 4 readers paging the whole history), tail under a flood (4 tailers vs a full-speed writer), wake-to-delivery latency (pings issued only once every tailer is parked in await_watermark_past), and hot multi-stream read_stream paging.

Eight metrics, prefix engine.live_tail. Six floors seeded loose in floors.json; the two derived ratios (catchup_scaling, writer_retention) are recorded but not gated, following bn-1dlb which left writer_retention ungated for the same variance reason.

Points worth a reviewer's attention:

1. Cursor advancement. Every loop follows mess-store/src/subscription.rs exactly: read_global_page(cursor-1), advance to max(last.global_position+1, frontier), treat an empty page with a moved frontier as keep-reading rather than caught-up, and never jump to the watermark. The corpus registers gap_streams one-record streams at even intervals so registry holes are spread through the whole scanned range instead of bunching in the first round-robin cycle. Every read pass asserts its exact delivered count, so a frontier bug fails rather than reporting a throughput win.

2. Why pass 3 exists. Pass 2 cannot measure the caught-up path. This engine commits far faster than the read path materialises, so a flooding writer leaves tailers permanently behind; the first cut of this workload recorded 4 parks total across 4 tailers. Pass 3 waits for every tailer to be parked before each single-record ping and puts the writer's pre-append timestamp in the payload, so the sample is exact and needs no shared slot.

3. Termination. Structural, not a stop flag or a count: the writer appends to a sentinel stream and a tailer exits on delivering that record. No tailer can be left parked on a watermark that will never advance.

4. The one bounded wait is wait_all_parked, 5ms, on the main thread outside the runtime. It is a safety valve, not a poll: if it expires the ping still goes out and that one sample is merely optimistic.

5. CLI --only / list-workloads. Added so a single workload can be measured without a ten-workload pass on a shared host. run_all is now a wrapper over run_selected and the settle placement moved from after-each-step to before-each-step-but-the-first, which is the identical pause pattern when nothing is filtered. A narrowed run is a measurement not a gate; the binary prints a NOTE and the README says the nightly gate must never pass it. Two new tests guard the selector, including one asserting every WORKLOAD_NAMES entry matches a step arm.

6. Floors were seeded under ambient load from two sibling workers (loadavg 1.39-1.59 one-minute). Noted in every source field. Load depresses a throughput reading, which makes a min floor looser, the safe direction, but the numbers are explicitly not quiet-host numbers.

Evidence: cargo test -p mess-bench 4 passed; cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean; just fmt-check clean; one full-mode gated run PASS on all 20 floor-gated metrics.

data.body:
Fixed in 335626a. compare_report() returns matched/total alongside regressions; compare() is now a thin wrapper so no existing caller changed. run_compare prints the historical string byte-identically when matched == total, and a distinct PASS (narrowed) line otherwise. Verified against the ledgers already on disk (no benchmark re-run):

PASS: all 20 floor-gated metrics within tolerance of crates/mess-bench/floors.json
PASS (narrowed): 6 of 20 floor-gated metrics checked; 14 absent from this ledger - NOT a full gate.

(em dash before NOT in the real output). Both exit 0; the string is the guard.

Test compare_pass_line_never_claims_a_full_gate_a_narrowed_ledger_did_not_run pins both through the real binary (CARGO_BIN_EXE_mess-bench, crafted floors + two ledgers) and asserts the narrowed output never contains 'PASS: all'. README --only section and the run_selected doc caveat now name both strings; the --only NOTE tells the operator which line to expect.

cargo test -p mess-bench 5 passed. cargo check --workspace --all-targets exit 0. just fmt-check exit 0.
